sentences.text:
This Criminal Original Petition has been filed seeking to quash the impugned private complaint in C.C.No.654 of 2022, on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate No.II, Ramanathapuram, filed by the respondent, alleging offences punishable under Sections 120(b), 341, 362, 384, 420, and 506(i)
of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

2. The allegation in the impugned private complaint is that the respondent had entered into a sale agreement with one Ajmal Khan for the sale of a property, which allegedly belongs to the respondent and the other legal heirs of the respondents father; that the respondent had received a sum of Rs.95,00,000/- as advance from the said Ajmal Khan and handed over the same to the petitioners,
who are closely related to the respondent; that the petitioners had misappropriated the said sum;
that a suit was filed by the said Ajmal Khan in O.S.No.1170 of 2020 before the City Civil Court,
Chennai, seeking specific performance and a temporary injunction restraining the respondent from alienating the property; that the City Civil Court had granted a temporary injunction; that the respondent, at the instigation of the petitioners and suppressing the said injunction order,
_____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/10/2025 02:47:12 pm ) had sold the property to third parties; and that thereafter, the petitioners had forced the respondent to register another property in favour of the second petitioner, who had not paid the sale consideration, and thus, all the petitioners have committed the aforesaid offences.
3.

The learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the respondent himself had violated the interim injunction order granted by the City Civil Court and had sold the property in favour of third parties, receiving a sale consideration of more than Rs.45,00,000/- in his account; that the other allegation, namely that he was forced to execute the sale deed in favour of the second petitioner, is an afterthought, as the alleged sale deed was executed on 16.11.2019, whereas the complaint was filed only on 20.06.2022; that the allegations only disclose a monetary dispute between close relatives; and that, therefore, the impugned private complaint is liable to be quashed.

4. The learned counsel for the respondent would vehemently oppose the prayer sought for by the petitioners for quashing the private complaint and would submit that the respondent was forced to violate the interim injunction order passed by the City Civil Court; that the petitioners had _____________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 13/10/2025 02:47:12 pm )
committed the offence of misappropriating the advance amount paid by the said Ajmal Khan; that the sale consideration for another property of the respondent, worth about Rs.1,80,00,000/-, was not paid to the respondent by the second petitioner; and that the points raised by the petitioners can be adjudicated only before the learned Judicial Magistrate, and hence, this petition is liable to be dismissed.
5.

The allegations in the private complaint would show that the respondent had entered into a sale agreement with one Ajmal Khan in respect of a property which is said to have been inherited by him from his father.
Admittedly, the respondent was not the exclusive owner of the said property.

In the suit in O.S.No.1170 of 2020 filed by the agreement holder, Ajmal Khan, the City Civil Court had granted an interim injunction order restraining the alienation of the suit property, even as per the Mohamed Ibrahim vs Abdullah Sahib on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185758625/
2 averments made in the impugned private complaint.

According to the respondent, he was forced by the petitioners to violate the said injunction order and to execute a sale deed in favour of one H.Mohammed Saleem and M.Rameesh Fathima, which was registered as Document No.225 of 2020, dated 15.10.2020, in violation of the said injunction order.
It is seen that a sum of R s . 4 5 , 0 0 , 0 0 0 / - w a s c r e d i t e d t o t h e a c c o u n t o f t h e
_ _ _ _ _ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 13/10/2025 02:47:12 pm ) respondent.
The respondent has suppressed all these facts in the private complaint.
6. The other allegation is that the respondent was forced to execute a sale deed in favour of his son-in-law, the second petitioner herein, and had executed the same on 06.11.2019.
However, the complaint was filed only on 20.06.2022.
The parties are closely related to each other.
The allegations, at best, reveal a monetary dispute between the parties.
The respondent himself, in the complaint, has stated that he had violated the interim injunction order passed by the City Civil Court.
The complaint cannot be entertained at the instance of such a person.
7. For all the aforesaid reasons, the impugned private complaint is an abuse of the process of law and is, therefore, liable to be quashed, and is accordingly quashed.
Thus, this Criminal Original Petition is allowed.
Consequently, the connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
